_about: The CER procedures run (kb/_cer_procedures.py): what each procedure settled and held, and the titles that need a person. A pre-fill no reason holds saves under its procedure (Open Asks Sheet 94 card 2); a held one pre-fills the tab and waits for a person.

procedures.name: Brand families join the family
procedures.rule: A title that names a known credential family (College Board AP and CLEP exams, a house family already in the reference) joins that family's title, with the family's issuer. An AP title, for an AP course, an AP exam or AP prep, takes College Board's official exam name, current or retired, whatever score, area, course code or school the college added and however it wrote the letters (A, AB, A/B, A+B or none); a title naming two exams waits for a person. An IB title takes IB's own subject name with its level, current or retired (IB Language A: Literature HL, IB Language A1 HL), HL where the college wrote none and SL for a subject IB offers at SL alone; the language the exam was written in folds into the subject, and a Language A exam in a language other than English carries (Non-English). A CLEP title takes College Board's exam name, one credential per exam: a world language exam's levels fold into it as score bands (CLEP Spanish Language), the numbered exams take Arabic numerals with no period subtitle (CLEP History of the United States 1), a renamed exam takes its current name (CLEP Information Systems) and a retired one keeps its own (CLEP Trigonometry).

source.words: it would be helpful to have a procedure that pre-seeds the common exhibit titles and issuing agencies -- all the APs should be an easy win, right?

procedures.name: The statewide catalog names it
procedures.rule: A title that matches an exhibit in MAP's statewide CCC-collaborative catalog takes that exhibit's title and issuer.

source.words: use the MAP statewide CRs to match some of the exhibits

procedures.name: NCCER keeps its own names
procedures.rule: An NCCER title keeps NCCER's catalog naming, levels and all, and NCCER issues it.

source.words: his NCCER Welding Level 1 family (house precedent)

procedures.name: Contractor classifications stay as written
procedures.rule: A California contractor classification (C-20, Class A) keeps its code and name, and the Contractors State License Board (CSLB) issues it.

source.words: kept verbatim per Rule 8b, the issuer-assigned code

procedures.name: Apprenticeships take the trade's house name
procedures.rule: A carpentry journeyman certificate, a Carpenters trade apprenticeship or an Ironworkers period takes the house shape for its trade, with the joint apprenticeship committee the Division of Apprenticeship Standards names as issuer.

source.words: the Journeyman Certificate- Apprenticeship Carpentry family and the DIR DAS carpenter page (occupation 2180)

procedures.name: One-off titles decided once
procedures.rule: A title a session or curator already decided by hand, with its reasoning, keeps that decision.

source.words: each with its reasoning receipted in the note

procedures.name: A course names its own exam
procedures.rule: A credit-by-exam, portfolio or course-coded title takes the course's Common Course Number title, then its C-ID title, then the college's own course title, never the mechanism; California Community Colleges issues it. A title that names a school or district goes to the classifier, because the school issues it (Rule 5f).

source.words: Sam's Cx procedure: CCN title, then C-ID, then the course's own title

procedures.name: A high school course takes its college course's name
procedures.rule: A high school, district, county office or ROP articulation takes the name of the college course it is aligned to (its Common Course Number title, then its C-ID title, then its M-ID title, then the college's own course title), and the school, district or county office the classifier named issues it. An AP or other exam keeps its own name. A title with no aligned course that shares a word with it, or with no named issuer, stays with a person.

source.words: Make it a rule (Open Asks Sheet 147 card 2: 'High school and ROP titles: settle the 96 under one rule, with the AP exams keeping their names?'); 2026-10-30: 'if there's a M-ID title aligned show it and let it determine the proposed classifyer'

procedures.name: The issuer issues the card
procedures.rule: The issuing agency is the body that issues the credential, never the college, school or employer that teaches toward it. OSHA cards are issued by U.S. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), under that exact name.

source.words: they would not be the issuing agency, osha would.
source.also: Open Asks Sheet 39 card 2 (2026-10-05): the OSHA issuer's name across the CER

procedures.name: A named school is the agency
procedures.rule: A high school, ROP, adult school or noncredit provider named in the title comes out of the title and becomes the issuing and training agency; a real outside issuer (PLTW) is never replaced by the school. A title that says high school without naming one takes Local High School as issuer.

source.words: strip the school, make it the agency

procedures.name: Level words go last
procedures.rule: A leading Beginning, Intermediate or Advanced moves to the end of the title; Intro becomes Introduction; an official proper name keeps its own order. A world-language level leads instead (language-levels).

source.words: level words move to the end of the title

procedures.name: Name the ASE test
procedures.rule: An automotive course exhibit that prepares for an ASE test names the test in parentheses after the title, with its code and official name: Automotive Technology (ASE A7 Heating and Air Conditioning). A course code names a test only when the course's own title agrees with it (Las Positas's AUTO P1 is Powertrains, not the parts test). The ASE certification itself keeps its own name (ASE A7 — Heating and Air Conditioning).

source.words: Auto exhibits are most often aligned with ASE cert titles and I started adding those to later exhibit titles in parens after the title

procedures.name: Level numerals are Arabic
procedures.rule: A level numeral is 1, 2, 3, never I, II, III. An official name that carries a Roman numeral keeps it (State Fire Training's Firefighter I, Fire Officer, Fire Inspector).

source.words: Many exhibits use I, II, III and I skipped adjusting some of those to 1,2,3 for consistency.

procedures.name: World-language levels
procedures.rule: A world-language course is Elementary or Intermediate, then the language, then 1 or 2, the level word first as C-ID names these courses: Elementary Spanish 1, Intermediate Spanish 2. Course 1 and 2 (or 1A and 1B), Beginning and High-Beginning are Elementary 1 and 2; 2A and 2B are Intermediate 1 and 2.

source.words: look for beginning labels that should be elementary (our canonical term for 1,2 or 1A,1B and intermediate should be often 2,3 or 2A,2B

procedures.name: How it was assessed never splits a credential
procedures.rule: Exam, portfolio, challenge and similar method words collapse into one credential; an industry certification and a local course exam stay apart; a narrower competency never folds into a broader one.

source.words: the credential-merge doctrine: what folds and what stays distinct

procedures.name: Join, and let faculty pull out
procedures.rule: When two titles likely name one credential and Rule 8c does not keep them apart, give them one title; faculty may pull them apart later.

source.words: it is better to over merge and give faculty the chance to pull them out rather than the other way around. It's easier to respond to a decision than to make one.

procedures.name: The classifier decides the rest
procedures.rule: Every title no rule settles goes to the classifier, which reads the skill and every procedure above.

source.words: have you classify and complete common exhibit titles
